stories.title: Config overlay persistence + layered read (config.json default <- Pi-local overlay override)
acceptance: [ATLAS DESIGN-GATE -- load-bearing config/SSOT seam] introduce a Pi-local OVERLAY file (gitignored, added to deploy-pi.sh rsync excludes like .env so deploy never clobbers it) that layers OVER config.json: effective = overlay-override ELSE config.json default. config.json stays read-only shipped default; nothing writes config.json at runtime

[GAP 2 -- A-4 SSOT, Atlas] the overlay merge is ONE shared utility in src/common/config/ (e.g. resolveEffectiveConfig(base, overlay, allowlist)) that BOTH config readers call -- the orchestrator loadConfigWithSecrets AND states_http_server._loadDisplaySection (which reads config.json directly). Effective config MUST be identical for every consumer (avoids the A-4 divergence). Allow-list enforced at BOTH read (overlay keys outside the allow-list ignored + logged) AND write (US-531 endpoint) = defense-in-depth

[GAP 3a -- one key one truth, Atlas] do NOT mint a new pi.display.carousel.autoRotate bool. The overlay stores the EXISTING pi.display.carousel.autoRotateS (seconds; 0=off, >0=on). The UI toggle derives on/off from autoRotateS>0 (off writes 0, on writes the shipped interval)

overridable-key allow-list (Slice 1): pi.display.carousel.autoRotateS, pi.power.mode, pi.alerts.audioAlerts, pi.calibration.mode, pi.analysis.triggerAfterDrive. pi.power.mode overlay value MUST validate to {car,wall,unknown} -- invalid -> unknown (honest-unknown contract), never a confident wrong mode
honest-instrument: malformed/absent overlay -> config.json default, never a guessed value; out-of-allow-list key ignored + logged

test proves: overlay override wins over default via the SHARED resolver for BOTH read paths; absent overlay -> default; out-of-allow-list key rejected; autoRotateS 0<->interval round-trips; deploy-exclude keeps the overlay across an rsync; ruff clean

validationCriteria.outcome: both readers return 0 after the deploy (overlay preserved + wins for every consumer -- no divergence)

conditionalOutcomes: Atlas ruled the overlay contract sound 2026-08-03 (3 gaps folded). resolveEffectiveConfig is the single seam; do not merge the overlay per-reader.

stories.completionNotes:
OVERLAY CONTRACT AS BUILT: flat dot-path map (config.local.json) beside config.json; effective = allow-listed overlay override ELSE config.json default. Flat keys were the deliberate choice -- they make the allow-list a LITERAL key comparison, so US-531's write gate can reuse validateOverlayValue() unchanged instead of writing a second recursive walk that would drift from this one. US-531: import validateOverlayValue + overlayPathFor from common.config.overlay; do NOT re-implement the allow-list.

GAP 2 (A-4 SSOT) SATISFIED AND MUTATION-PROVEN, NOT ASSERTED. Both readers call applyConfigOverlay. The load-bearing test is test_bothReadPaths_agreeOnEffectiveAutoRotateS -- parametrized [0, 8, 20] because 8 equals the shipped default and would stay GREEN under a broken reader. Mutation A (drop the seam from _loadDisplaySection) -> 3 red, and test_loadConfigWithSecrets_appliesOverlay STAYED GREEN: a per-reader test suite would ship the exact A-4 divergence this story exists to prevent. Mutation B (drop it from loadConfigWithSecrets) -> 4 red. Both reverted by hand (git checkout is outside the allow-list) and re-verified green.

HONEST BOUND ON test_bothReadPaths_agreeOnRejectingAnOutOfAllowListKey: it cannot detect a missing seam, because a rejected key leaves BOTH readers on the default either way. It pins the rejection, not the wiring. The autoRotateS parity test is the one that pins the wiring -- do not delete it as redundant.

GAP 3a HONOURED: no pi.display.carousel.autoRotate bool was minted. autoRotateS (0=off, >0=on) is the only key; US-532's toggle derives on/off from >0 and writes 0 / the shipped interval.

HONEST-INSTRUMENT, MECHANISM-PINNED: invalid pi.power.mode coerces to 'unknown' (NOT to the config.json default -- a corrupt mode means the deployment context is unknown, and base could legitimately ship 'car'). Mutation C (fall back to default instead of coercing) -> 6 red; note the WARNING log still said 'resolving to unknown' while the code no longer did, i.e. the log is a DECLARATION and only the assertion pins the MECHANISM. Out-of-allow-list keys are ignored + logged and never invent a config branch (proven against the REAL config.json: a planted pi.obd.port override raised KeyError('obd') = nothing created). Wrong-typed values fall back to the default; bool is explicitly excluded from the numeric check so True cannot pass as autoRotateS.

DEPLOY DURABILITY -- THE TAR FALLBACK HAD A SECOND HOLE. deploy-pi.sh has TWO sync paths. Excluding config.local.json from the tarball is NOT sufficient: the fallback wipes the remote top level BEFORE extracting, so the overlay also needed a `! -name` entry in the preserve find. Excluding from the tarball alone would have silently deleted the operator's settings on any deploy from a machine without rsync. All three edits landed + tested separately.

REAL-CONFIG SMOKE (dev box, beyond the synthetic fixtures): planted an overlay next to the SHIPPED config.json -> both readers returned autoRotateS=0, power.mode=wall, pi.obd.port rejected+logged ONCE PER READER (both gates fire). `git status --ignored` confirmed `!!` on config.local.json -- git ACTUALLY ignores it, not merely a .gitignore line. Artifacts removed; tree clean.

STILL OWED BY THE VALIDATION CRITERIA -- DO NOT READ GREEN AS DONE: the AC's 'overlay survives an rsync' is asserted against deploy-pi.sh TEXT, not a real rsync. The real proof is the PM's Pi deploy: set autoRotateS=0 in /home/mcornelison/Projects/Eclipse-01/config.local.json, deploy, confirm the file still exists and BOTH readers return 0. Also note a carousel-config change needs an eclipse-states-http bounce (injected + cached at startup -- US-533 GAP 1 / US-536 deploy note).

BLAST RADIUS: loadConfigWithSecrets is the project-wide config entry point, so this is a base-module change -- PM should run the FULL suite at integration. In-loop I ran the story file (42) + the consumer suites of both touched readers: 360 passed, 1 skipped (test_token.py:70 POSIX file-mode gate on Windows -- PRE-EXISTING, documented by US-525, not mine). ruff clean on all 4 .py files; `bash -n deploy/deploy-pi.sh` clean (pytest cannot see a shell syntax error); validate_config.py passes through the new seam. Behaviour is a strict no-op when no overlay file exists, which is the shipped state.

TD-075 still stands: `ruff check src/ tests/` exits 1 on a clean tree (10 project-wide errors in src/calibration/speed_aligner-spool.py + tests/pm/*), so lint was per-touched-file. `make` is NOT on PATH here -- `make lint` exits 127, which READS LIKE A PASS.

FOR PM: a new inbox item appeared during this iteration whose filename names US-536's subject (Atlas RCA on --disable-gpu crashing the renderer). Not my lane to read -- flagging only because disposition-B (US-536) REVERTS --disable-gpu and this may bear on it. Read it before dispatching US-536.

stories.completionNotes:
ENDPOINT AS BUILT: POST /settings, body {key, value}. Token gate FIRST (_tokenOk, reused verbatim -- never weakened, and the Bearer form still works because I did not read the header myself). Then: no configPath wired -> honest 503; malformed/non-object body or missing key/value -> 400; key not on the allow-list -> 403; value fails its type rule -> 400; write failure -> 500. NO WRITE on every rejection path, asserted file-absence not just status code.

I TOOK US-530'S HANDOFF EXACTLY: zero new validation. The endpoint imports overlay.OVERRIDABLE_KEYS + overlay.validateOverlayValue. The atomic write lives in common.config.overlay (writeOverlayValue), NOT in the HTTP layer -- same posture as US-403 delegating its gate to service_control, so the server stays a thin transport and a future non-HTTP writer gets the identical gate.

HONEST RESPONSE IS A RE-READ, NOT AN ECHO. After writing, the endpoint calls readEffectiveValue(configPath, key) which reloads config.json + the overlay and resolves through applyConfigOverlay -- so it reports what the orchestrator and carousel will ACTUALLY see, including the power-mode coercion.

*** THE NON-ECHO TEST GAP I ALMOST SHIPPED -- CARRY THIS. *** My first suite pinned echo-vs-re-read ONLY on the failure path, because on a SUCCESSFUL write the stored value EQUALS the effective value, so an echoing endpoint passes every happy-path assertion. Narrow mutation (value: stored, keeping ok: wrote) proved it: 1 red, not 2. I added test_settingsWrite_storedButUnresolvable_reportsNullNotTheRequest -- a config.json whose pi.power branch is a STRING, so the write succeeds but the override cannot be resolved onto it and the honest answer is null. That is the ONE success-path case where the two implementations differ. GENERAL RULE, NEW SHAPE OF THE OLD ONE: when a response is supposed to be a RE-READ rather than an ECHO, the happy path cannot prove it -- you need a case where the stored value and the resolved value DISAGREE.

And it restated declaration-vs-mechanism again: under that mutation the WARNING log said 'Overlay key blocked by a non-dict branch' while the endpoint cheerfully returned 'wall'. The log told the truth; the response lied. Only the assertion caught it.

MUTATIONS RUN (all reverted BY HAND -- git checkout is outside the allow-list -- and re-verified green): (A) drop _tokenOk from the settings handler -> 2 red (401 + wrong-token). (B) replace overlay.OVERRIDABLE_KEYS with an endpoint-local tuple missing one key -> red on the parametrized case. (C) echo the request -> 2 red.

HONEST BOUND ON MUTATION B: parametrizing over OVERRIDABLE_KEYS catches DRIFT, not duplication -- an endpoint-local list that is currently IDENTICAL to the SSOT would still pass. It fails the moment the allow-list grows, which is the real risk (Slice 2 will add keys). I also assert _VALID_VALUES covers OVERRIDABLE_KEYS exactly, so a new key cannot land untested.

ATOMICITY IS PINNED AS A MECHANISM, NOT A COMMENT: test_overlayWriterUsesOsReplace_notATruncatingWrite spies os.replace and asserts the destination is the real path and the source is NOT -- a truncating open() of the live file would pass every other write test. Plus: a failing replace leaves the prior overlay BYTE-IDENTICAL, and leaves no .tmp behind. fsync before replace because the Pi loses power with the ignition.

MERGE, NOT CLOBBER: each save loads the current overlay and sets one key, so toggling one control cannot reset another (proven at both the module and endpoint level). A malformed existing overlay is REPLACED rather than appended to -- readers already ignore it entirely, so repairing it is the consistent outcome.

REAL-CONFIG SMOKE (beyond the fixtures, against the SHIPPED config.json): overlayPathFor('config.json') -> 'config.local.json'; authed autoRotateS=0 and power.mode=wall both 200 with real effective values; UNAUTHED write -> 401 AND the overlay still read 'wall' afterwards (the 401 wrote nothing -- absence of a side effect, not just a status code); pi.obd.port -> 403; config.json byte-unchanged. Artifact deleted, `git status --ignored` clean.

DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT -- NO GET COUNTERPART. The effective values already reach the dashboard via the injected config (US-506 window.DISPLAY_CAROUSEL), so a GET /settings would be a SECOND source for the same fact and could disagree with the injected one. US-532 should render from the injected config, not invent a read endpoint.

FOR US-533 (GAP 1): I did NOT bounce eclipse-states-http on an autoRotateS write -- that is explicitly US-533's acceptance, and doing it here would have put a service restart inside a story scoped to persistence. The seam is ready: the handler knows the key it just wrote. Remember the injected carousel config is cached at states-http STARTUP, so auto-rotate needs a bounce + page reload and must be labeled 'applies on restart', never claimed live.

GATE, SYNCHRONOUS, IN-LOOP, BEFORE THE COMMIT (no TD-059 stall): RED first for the right reason (ImportError: cannot import name 'getDotPath' -- feature genuinely absent, not a typo). Then 346 passed, 1 skipped across the 2 story files + tests/common/test_config_overlay.py + all of tests/pi/splash/ + tests/test_secrets_loader.py. The 1 skip is PRE-EXISTING (test_token.py:70 POSIX file-mode on Windows, same one US-525/528/530 documented). ruff clean on all 4 .py files. validate_config.py passes.

BLAST RADIUS FOR PM: this is a NEW WRITE SURFACE on the Pi, so it deserves the full suite at integration. It is additive -- the new route is the only behaviour change and every existing route/test is untouched (I did switch states_http_server to `from common.config import overlay` and call overlay.applyConfigOverlay; no test referenced the old bare import, checked before changing it).

LIVE VALIDATION OWED (do not read green as done): the AC's POST-with-token/POST-without-token drill is proven on the dev box against the real config.json, but NOT on the Pi through the kiosk's own fetch. The Pi proof is US-532/533's -- and it needs the states-http unit to be running with --config pointing at the deployed config.json (main() now passes configPath=args.config, so the existing unit file needs NO new argument).

ENVIRONMENT (unchanged from US-530, re-confirmed): `make` is NOT on PATH -- `make lint` exits 127, which READS LIKE A PASS. Used `python -m ruff check` per touched file; TD-075 still makes project-wide ruff exit 1 on a clean tree. The Bash tool rejects heredocs containing brace-with-quote (JSON literals) -- build dicts with dict() instead.

stories.completionNotes:
BAND AS BUILT: Iris Option B -- a Settings section at the TOP of the EXISTING US-403 setup-menu overlay, above OBD-II Services and Display/Exit. No 5th carousel card. Each of the 5 rows = label + honest apply-note + a segmented control; a toggle is a 2-choice segment (Off/On) and power mode a 3-choice one (CAR/WALL/UNKNOWN), so BOTH render through ONE mechanism -- and 'unknown' is expressible as NO choice selected, which is how an unreadable setting shows itself instead of defaulting to a confident Off.

READ PATH -- NO GET ENDPOINT, PER US-531'S RULING. The state server injects the 5 effective values as window.DISPLAY_SETTINGS through the same quoted-placeholder seam as __DISPLAY_CAROUSEL__/__DISPLAY_AUTODIM__, resolved via overlay.readEffectiveValue (the SAME seam the write route re-reads through). loadEffectiveSettings iterates overlay.OVERRIDABLE_KEYS rather than a local list, so a Slice-2 key reaches the band with NO server edit, and the INJECTED KEYS ARE THE POST BODY KEYS -- there is no display-side mapping table to drift from the write gate's allow-list.

*** THE DESIGN CALL THAT MATTERS: PER-REQUEST, NOT CACHED. *** The codebase already contains BOTH patterns and they are not interchangeable -- carouselConfig is resolved once at handler construction (US-506), while __DEPLOY_VERSION__ is resolved per request (US-501, whose comment explains it had to move because a startup-cached value is always one deploy stale). The settings band has the IDENTICAL failure mode: save autoRotateS=0 -> reload the page without bouncing the unit -> a cached blob renders 8 again, silently discarding a save that DID happen. So it follows US-501. Mutation B (cache it at construction) -> EXACTLY 1 red, and it was test_index_settingsAreResolvedPerRequest_notCachedAtConstruction -- confirming that docstring's own claim that every OTHER test in the file passes against the cached implementation.

I DELIBERATELY DID NOT FORCE PARITY WITH DISPLAY_CAROUSEL. After a save-without-bounce, DISPLAY_SETTINGS.autoRotateS (stored: 0) and DISPLAY_CAROUSEL.autoRotateS (running: 8) DISAGREE -- and that disagreement is TRUE, not a bug. The band reports what is STORED; the carousel is still running the value cached at its startup (Atlas GAP 1). A parity assertion here would have been the wrong instinct: it would force the band to report the stale running value, i.e. to hide the gap. The 'applies on restart' label is what makes the gap honest instead.

APPLY-STATE LABELS SHIP CONSERVATIVE ON EVERY ROW, AND THIS IS A DELIBERATE DEVIATION FROM IRIS'S TABLE -- READ THIS BEFORE US-533. Iris specced power mode / audio alerts as 'live' and triggerAfterDrive as 'next drive'. But an apply-state is a CLAIM ABOUT A CONSUMER, and US-532 wires NO consumer -- that is explicitly US-533's acceptance. A restart always applies an overlay value (every consumer re-reads config at process start), so 'applies on restart' can never be a lie; 'applies now' would be an over-promise, and the over-promise is the DANGEROUS direction because it is exactly the silent no-op this band exists to prevent (operator taps, label says it took effect, nothing changed). Under-promising costs only a needless restart. So all 5 rows read 'applies on restart', the note is DERIVED from a single {live, restart, next-drive} mapping, and US-533 flips `apply` per key as it wires + PROVES each consumer -- test_noRowClaimsLiveUntilItsConsumerIsWired will go red on purpose when it does, which is the intended handshake.

HONEST SAVE FLOW: tap -> 'saving…' (which repaints the CURRENTLY KNOWN stored value, NOT the requested one -- painting the request during the pending state is the optimistic success Iris ruled out wearing a nicer label) -> repaint from settingsSaveResult(res).value, the server's RE-READ. A body with no `value` at all (401, network failure, non-JSON) yields null = Unknown, because we genuinely do not know what is stored. No control confirms -- these are reversible preferences, and borrowing the service-control confirm would train the operator to dismiss the modal that guards a service Stop.

ONE PAINT PATH PER ROW. The row is painted by a single `render` closure, built once per row, called for the initial paint AND handed to the save handler for the repaint. That is stronger than two call sites agreeing: if the save handler painted the row itself it could paint the requested value while the open path paints the stored one, and the UI would disagree with ITSELF across a page reload.

MUTATIONS RUN (all 5 reverted BY HAND -- git checkout is outside the allow-list -- and re-verified green): (A) repaint from the request instead of out.value -> 1 red. (B) cache settings at construction -> 1 red. (C) coerce bools truthily so unresolvable reads as Off -> 3 red. (D) drift one display key from the allow-list -> 4 red. (E) drop the X-Splash-Token header -> 1 red.

*** HONEST BOUND ON MUTATION A -- CARRY THIS TO US-533. *** The optimistic-echo mutation was caught by SOURCE INSPECTION ONLY. The pure non-echo tests (settingsSaveResult given a response whose value DISAGREES with the request) all stayed GREEN, because they exercise the reducer in isolation and the DOM is free to ignore its answer. There is no DOM harness in this kit -- the node probe evaluates pure exports with no document -- so every 'the wiring actually applies the policy' guard in this suite is a source-text assertion, exactly like US-490's. That is a real ceiling, not a defect I can close inside this story: the reducer is provably honest, and the guard that the DOM USES the reducer is textual. US-533 adding a live round-trip on the Pi is what closes it.

I ALSO KEPT US-531'S NON-ECHO LESSON ON THE DISPLAY SIDE: test_saveResult_takesTheServersValue_notTheRequestedOne uses the SAME disagreement fixture family -- ok:true but value:null (the write landed, the override could not resolve onto a non-dict branch). A success fixture where res.value equals the request cannot tell an honest implementation from an echoing one, which is how US-531 nearly shipped the bug.

CROSS-LANGUAGE SSOT GUARD (new shape): the display MUST carry its own copy of the key list -- it is a different runtime and cannot import the Python allow-list -- so the risk here is not duplication but DRIFT. test_settingsSpecs_coversTheOverlayAllowListExactly pins the JS list to overlay.OVERRIDABLE_KEYS in BOTH directions (order included), and the row/write tests are parametrized over the Python SSOT. This is strictly stronger than US-531's bound, which could not fail on a currently-identical local copy.

REAL-CONFIG SMOKE (against a COPY of the SHIPPED config.json, in tmp -- the repo tree was never written): injected effective = autoRotateS 8 / power unknown / audioAlerts false / calibration false / triggerAfterDrive true, keys == allow-list; POST autoRotateS=0 and power.mode=wall both 200; RE-SERVED the page with NO restart -> the band showed 0 + wall (the per-request property, proven live); UNAUTHED write -> 401 AND the overlay still read 'wall' afterwards; pi.obd.port -> 403; power.mode='moon-base' -> 400; still 'wall' after both rejections; config.json BYTE-UNCHANGED; tmp tree removed.

GATE, SYNCHRONOUS, IN-LOOP, BEFORE THE COMMIT (no TD-059 stall): RED first for the right reason (ImportError: cannot import name 'loadEffectiveSettings' -- feature genuinely absent). Then GREEN: 64 story tests, plus the full tests/ui/ suite (551) and tests/pi/splash/ + tests/common/test_config_overlay*.py + tests/deploy/test_dashboard_kit.py all clean. The 1 skip is PRE-EXISTING (test_token.py:70 POSIX file-mode on Windows, same one US-525/528/530/531 documented). ruff clean on all 3 .py files; validate_config.py passes.

BLAST RADIUS FOR PM: strictly ADDITIVE -- `git diff --numstat` shows 0 deletions across all 4 source files. No existing route, export, or CSS rule was modified; the band is a new section and DISPLAY_SETTINGS a new placeholder. The one behavioural change to an existing function is openMenu() also calling buildSettings(). Still worth the full suite at integration since states_http_server is on the Pi's serve path.

LIVE VALIDATION OWED (do not read green as done): the AC's 'open the setup-menu overlay on the Pi and view the Settings band' is proven on the dev box through the real HTTP server + the real config.json, but NOT on the Pi through the kiosk's own chromium. Needs a deploy + an eclipse-states-http bounce. Note for whoever validates: the ⋮ is PARKED-ONLY (US-490), so on a driving Pi use the 5s long-press.

ENVIRONMENT (re-confirmed, unchanged): `make` is NOT on PATH -- `make lint` exits 127, which READS LIKE A PASS; used `python -m ruff check` per touched file (TD-075 keeps project-wide ruff at exit 1). The Bash tool still rejects heredocs containing brace-with-quote (JSON object literals in inline python) -- build payloads with dict() / dict([(k, v)]) instead. NEW: writes outside the repo working dir are not permitted, so an ad-hoc smoke script must run via a heredoc rather than a temp file. ALSO NEW: `tests/ui/` + `tests/pi/splash/` together exceed the 120s Bash default on this SMB share -- pass an explicit timeout or the run is backgrounded (which is the TD-059 trap; I read the completed output file in-iteration rather than letting the result be lost).

stories.completionNotes:
*** PROVENANCE -- READ FIRST, IT BOUNDS EVERY CLAIM BELOW. *** I did NOT write most of this code. A PRIOR ITERATION implemented US-533 and died before committing; I found the work UNCOMMITTED in the working tree (16 files) and my job this iteration was to verify, complete and land it. That is the 'check git head before retrying' lesson paying off -- re-implementing from scratch would have discarded good work. What I can personally attest to is listed under VERIFIED BY ME. What I CANNOT attest to is the RED-first history of the prior iteration's tests: I did not watch them fail against absent source. I substituted mutation testing, which for this purpose is the stronger evidence anyway (RED-first proves a test COULD fail; mutation proves it fails for THE RIGHT REASON), but the distinction is real and I am not going to paper over it.

WHAT I ACTUALLY CHANGED THIS ITERATION: one line. `from common.config import overlay` was an unused import in tests/pi/splash/test_states_http_carousel_per_request.py -- the sole ruff error across all 16 files. I checked it was genuinely vestigial rather than a lost drift guard before deleting it (the file writes its overlay through the REAL POST /settings route, which is better than importing the module).

AS BUILT -- B1 (CIO-ratified path #3): pi.display.carousel is now resolved PER REQUEST in _injectHtml, joining __DEPLOY_VERSION__ (US-501) and __DISPLAY_SETTINGS__ (US-532). It was the LAST resolved-at-construction value in that method. This DELETES the eclipse-states-http restart requirement instead of authorising it -- the bounce is polkit-denied by design (BL-030 B1), so a restart-based toggle would have been a silent no-op on the Pi while passing every dev-box test. carouselConfig is KEPT as the fallback for servers constructed with no configPath, so US-506 behaviour is intact where there is no file to re-read. The band triggers the reload itself (SETTINGS_RELOAD_DELAY_MS=700) and the row says 'applies on reload'.

AS BUILT -- B2: pi.alerts.audioAlerts removed from the allow-list. One deletion, and the row vanishes from the band, the injected read AND the write gate, because all three derive from that list -- which is exactly the payoff US-530/531/532 were built for. The key still exists as a config DEFAULT in obdii/config/loader.py:142; that is correct and deliberate (it is a config key, just not an operator-overridable one). Audio remains US-538.

AS BUILT -- power mode is genuinely LIVE: OverlayConfigPowerModeSource re-reads the effective key on every acquire() through the US-530 seam, wired via PowerModeProvider.fromConfigPath and a configPath threaded main -> createOrchestratorFromConfig -> ApplicationOrchestrator -> card-state emitter. No path (standalone composers) falls back to the US-421 snapshot source: degrade to STALE, never to no power tile.

APPLY-STATES ARE NOW ONLY ONES A CONSUMER EARNED, and the US-532 handshake fired as designed. US-532 deliberately shipped 'applies on restart' on every row and left test_noRowClaimsLiveUntilItsConsumerIsWired to go RED on purpose when the consumers landed. It did. The map is re-cut to {live, reload, capture-restart} with NO unused entries (test_noDeadApplyStatesAreLeftInTheMapping pins that -- an unused label is one nobody has checked against a consumer, and the next story reaches for it as if someone had). Calibration/auto-analyze say 'applies on capture restart' rather than the bare 'restart' US-532 shipped: that label was TRUE but useless, because the only unit this band talks to (states-http) is the wrong one to restart. Naming the service is the difference between honest and merely not-false.

*** VERIFIED BY ME -- MUTATION, NOT ASSERTION. *** Three mutations, each applied by hand, run, and reverted BY HAND (git checkout is outside the allow-list), with the reverts confirmed byte-exact via `git diff --numstat` before committing:
(A) force the emitter to always use fromConfig (drop the live branch) -> 2 RED, and critically one of them is BEHAVIOURAL (getPowerMode() returns 'car' after an overlay write of 'wall'), not merely an isinstance check. A type-only guard would have been the weaker test.
(B) revert the carousel to construction-cached -> 5 RED, headed by the story test test_autoRotateSWrite_isServedWithoutARestart (one running server, POST, re-serve -- no bounce, no re-construction). That test is the whole of B1.
(C) drop the `ok` conjunct from settingsReloadNeeded -> 2 RED, including test_reloadDecisionUsesTheSaveResult_notTheRawResponse, whose fixture uses a TRUTHY-BUT-NOT-TRUE `ok: 'yes'` -- the non-echo discipline US-531/532 established, carried correctly into the reload decision. Reloading after a rejected write would wipe the error note and repaint the unchanged value, which READS AS SUCCESS; that is the exact silent no-op the band exists to prevent, so it is the right thing to pin hardest.

*** THE HONEST BOUND ON THE WIRING CHAIN -- CARRY THIS. *** The emitter half is proven behaviourally, but the LAST HOP is not. test_card_power_mode_live_wiring pins main() with `assert 'configPath=args.config' in source` plus inspect.signature checks on runWorkflow/createOrchestratorFromConfig/ApplicationOrchestrator, and it drives a _FakeOrch rather than a real ApplicationOrchestrator. So the claim 'the deployed Pi builds the LIVE source' rests on a source-text assertion at the main() end -- the same declaration-vs-mechanism family this sprint has hit four times running. It is defensible (main() is hard to drive in-process) but it is NOT behavioural, and if the power tile still reads stale on the Pi this is the first place to look, not the last.

GATE, SYNCHRONOUS, IN-LOOP, BEFORE THE COMMIT (no TD-059 stall): 618 tests across tests/common/test_config_overlay*.py + tests/pi/power/ + the new orchestrator wiring file + ALL of tests/pi/splash/ + tests/ui/test_carousel_settings_band.py + tests/ui/test_carousel_settings_apply.py -- all passed, 1 skipped. The 1 skip is PRE-EXISTING (test_token.py:70 POSIX file-mode gate on Windows, documented by US-525/528/530/531/532). Re-run GREEN after all three mutation reverts. ruff clean on all 16 touched files (after my one-line fix); validate_config.py passes.

NO SEPARATE AD-HOC SMOKE THIS TIME, DELIBERATELY: prior F-126 stories ran one because their tests used synthetic fixtures. These do not -- test_states_http_carousel_per_request.py boots a REAL StatesHttpServer on a real port and drives a REAL authenticated POST /settings, so the round-trip is already exercised end to end through the production code path. A hand-rolled smoke would have been strictly weaker than the suite.

BLAST RADIUS FOR PM -- BIGGER THAN THE PRIOR F-126 STORIES, RUN THE FULL SUITE. Unlike US-532 (0 deletions, purely additive), this one MODIFIES base modules on the Pi's hot path: ApplicationOrchestrator.__init__ and createOrchestratorFromConfig gained a parameter, main.runWorkflow gained a parameter, and the card-state emitter's provider construction changed. All three are backward-compatible (configPath defaults to None -> prior behaviour), which is why the ~80 orchestrator test files that build configs still pass -- but 'defaults preserve behaviour' is exactly the kind of claim a full suite exists to check.

LIVE VALIDATION OWED -- DO NOT READ GREEN AS DONE. The validationCriteria are Pi-side: toggle auto-rotate in the band, let the UI reload, confirm the carousel actually picks up the new period WITH NO states-http restart; set power mode to wall and confirm the power tile follows within one emit cycle; reboot and confirm both survive via the overlay. Nothing on the dev box can prove the polkit half of B1 -- that was BL-030's whole lesson (a capability the test kit cannot see is still a capability), and it cuts both ways: the dev box also cannot prove we no longer NEED the privilege. Deploy needs the dashboard kit + the Pi source; the states-http bounce that used to be required for a carousel-config change is now needed only for a code change.

ALSO STILL OUTSTANDING FOR PM (unchanged, not mine): three RED tests on the sprint branch, all US-536 fallout, all filed on I-us536 (the third appended by me during US-537). They must be retired before the full-suite integration gate means anything.

stories.completionNotes:
*** READ THE PREMISE CORRECTION FIRST -- IT CHANGES WHAT THIS STORY PROVES. *** AC-1 calls ribbon-pulse and stop-alarm-pulse 'always-on'. They were not. Both surfaces ship `hidden`, US-495's `[hidden] { display: none !important }` removes the box, and a display:none element runs NO animations. So neither pulse was burning a single frame on an idle bench Pi, and neither can have caused the US-522 freeze. I verified this by reading the cascade, not by assuming it -- and the existing test_dashboard_overlay_hidden_guard.py already pins the display:none result.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY ALWAYS-ON: `#track { will-change: transform }`. #track is a flex ROW holding every card side by side, so that hint promoted a full-width layer to the compositor and held the backing store for the entire session -- parked, idle, screen untouched -- and auto-rotate's transform transition landed straight on top of it. It is the ONLY unconditional GPU cost in the sheet and it is the change in this story most likely to matter. The 0.25s transition stays; the browser still promotes for the duration it actually runs, and now releases it.

SO WHY GATE THE ANIMATIONS AT ALL, HONESTLY: the pre-existing gate was the PAINT cascade -- the pulse was silenced only because an `!important` display rule outranked the ribbon's own `display: flex`. That is precisely the race US-495 LOST, when author `display` declarations beat the UA `[hidden]` sheet and five overlays painted at once. Gating motion on a rule that already failed once in this codebase is the fragile version. Both pulses now hang off the STATE attribute carousel.js owns in lockstep (`data-level` / `data-severity`), so re-losing the display race can no longer arm a phantom pulsing alert band across every card. Real hardening, correctly sized -- not the freeze fix.

THE JS HALF WAS A LATENT BUG, NOT JUST A REFACTOR: hideTakeover() set `hidden` but left `data-severity="stop"` behind forever, so the STOP alarm rule kept matching an ACKNOWLEDGED takeover. Inert today (no box), but it meant the CSS gate the existing test_stopTakeover_motionIsOnlyOnALiveStop asserts was true of the STYLESHEET and false of the DOM. Now the attribute drops with the surface, mirroring renderRibbon's existing data-level contract.

TESTS ARE RESOLVED THROUGH THE REAL CASCADE OVER THE REAL POST-JS DOM, not grepped. I used the US-499 render harness (render_harness.runDashboard boots the SHIPPED carousel.js over the SHIPPED markup; dashboardSurface resolves the SHIPPED stylesheet over what it leaves). NOTE FOR THE NEXT STORY -- I nearly missed this: US-532's completionNotes say 'there is no DOM harness in this kit', which is true of carousel_probe.js (pure exports, no document) but NOT of the kit as a whole. dom_probe.js + render_harness.py are a full DOM + cascade harness, and they turn US-532's stated source-inspection ceiling into a real mechanism assertion. Worth revisiting the US-532 band guards with it.

RED FIRST, FOR THE RIGHT REASONS: 6 of 13 failed against unmodified source, each naming the winning declaration and its selector -- `#dtc-ribbon { animation: ribbon-pulse ... }`, `#dtc-takeover[data-severity="stop"] { animation: stop-alarm-pulse ... }` on an ACKNOWLEDGED takeover, `#track { will-change: transform }`. The three production edits are therefore each proven RED-first; no post-hoc mutation was needed for them.

*** THE HOLE I FOUND BY MUTATING, WHICH A STOP-ONLY FIXTURE HIDES. *** My first ribbon guard used a single `stop` code. Mutation D (gate on `[data-level="stop"]` instead of `[data-level]`) ALSO silences the idle phantom and passed that guard -- while stranding WATCH/MINOR/UNKNOWN ribbons STATIC, silently deleting the motion channel for three of the four levels. Caught only after parametrizing over all four severities: 3 red, `stop` GREEN. GENERAL SHAPE, and it is the same family as US-530's 'never let the fixture value equal the default': when you TIGHTEN a gate, the fixture must cover the whole domain the gate used to admit, or an over-tight gate reads identical to a correct one. `ribbonView` sets `level: hero.severity` verbatim, so those four are the whole domain. Reverted by hand and re-verified green.

THE LOAD-BEARING TEST is test_motionIsDeclaredExactlyWhenTheSurfaceIsPainted -- animation-declared IFF painted, across 3 real lifecycle states x 2 surfaces, driven through the real poll and the real click handlers. Asserting 'the animation is gated' and 'the surface is hidden' separately lets the two drift apart (the US-530 assert-the-AGREEMENT lesson); this cannot pass unless they move together, and it covers the direction the story is NOT about -- gating so hard a live alert renders static. Its acknowledged-stop row deliberately expects the RIBBON to keep pulsing: acknowledging drops the takeover TO the ribbon, so the alert is still real.

HONEST BOUND ON test_everyAnimationDeclaration_isStateQualified: it is a SOURCE-TEXT sweep, stated as such in its own docstring. It cannot prove a qualifier is the RIGHT one -- the harness tests do that for the two surfaces that exist today. Its job is to fail the day a third infinite animation is added to a base rule, which no per-surface test can see. Also mutation-checked the two 'cheap fix' guards so they are not vacuous: deleting #track's transition -> red; deleting/narrowing the ribbon animation -> red.

GATE, SYNCHRONOUS, IN-LOOP, BEFORE THE COMMIT (no TD-059 stall): 698 collected across tests/ui/ + tests/deploy/test_dashboard_kit.py, 695 passed, 3 FAILED -- and all 3 are PRE-EXISTING US-536 fallout, none mine. Verified rather than asserted: `git log -1 -- config.json` and `-- dashboard.service.wayland` both return 3e67e5d (US-536), and my diff opens neither file. Two were already filed as I-us536; the THIRD (tests/ui/test_carousel_nav_model.py::test_configJson_carriesTheCarouselSection, `assert 0 == 8` -- config.json now ships autoRotateS:0 per US-536 AC-2) was NOT, so I appended it to that issue with a suggested disposition rather than opening a duplicate or fixing it in someone else's lane. ruff clean on the new test file.

LIVE VALIDATION OWED -- AND THIS ONE IS THE WHOLE STORY, DO NOT READ GREEN AS DONE. AC-2/AC-3 are Pi-side runtime measurements: with GPU on and auto-rotate ON, sustain carousel navigation for several minutes and confirm `journalctl -u eclipse-dashboard | grep -c AllocateRingBuffer` stays ~0 with chromium CPU low. NOTHING on the dev box can stand in for that -- same lesson as BL-030's 'a capability the test kit cannot see is still a capability'. And because of the premise correction above, if the freeze DOES reproduce with auto-rotate on, the animations were never the cause and the remaining suspects are the transform transitions themselves plus whatever else auto-rotate wakes; the will-change removal is the only load-bearing change here. Deploy note: this is a dashboard-kit change, so it needs the kit deployed; a carousel-config change additionally needs an eclipse-states-http bounce (US-536 deploy note), but nothing in THIS story touches injected config.

ENVIRONMENT (re-confirmed, unchanged): `make` is NOT on PATH -- `make lint` exits 127, WHICH READS LIKE A PASS; used `python -m ruff check` per touched file (TD-075 keeps project-wide ruff at exit 1 on a clean tree). tests/ui/ + tests/deploy/ exceed the Bash 120s default on this SMB share -- passed an explicit timeout and blocked on the result. Also: pytest's `N passed` summary line is suppressed by this repo's pytest config, so counts came from `--collect-only` plus the FAILED list; `| tail` alone can look like a clean run when it is not.
